notes: Component-routing + contract evals for the composition architecture. Cases 0–2 are adapted from the MIT-licensed anthropics/html-effectiveness set; they test that the run routes each content type to the right COMPONENT (or whole-page pattern) AND meets the shared contract. Case 3 tests long-form composition with pre-rendered mermaid; case 4 tests markdown-file rendering with an ASCII→Excalidraw conversion; case 5 tests diff/PR-review routing. Assertions with a "check" field are graded by scripts/grade_artifact.py; the rest need an LLM/human grader (routing quality, layout judgment, diagram fidelity). The scripted checks cover source-level correctness only — visual + interactive correctness in BOTH themes (code-surface flip, no overlapping diagram shapes, working interactions, clean console) still needs a browser QA pass. See evals/README.md for the full loop.

shared_assertions.text: Output is a single self-contained .html file (inline CSS+JS, no external CSS/JS/images, no CDN beyond the sanctioned Excalidraw embed)
Light + dark ship via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) following the OS automatically — no theme toggle, no [data-theme], no localStorage theme code
Embeds an agent-readable source mirror (<script type="text/markdown" id="artifact-source">) holding the content as markdown

Passes `python scripts/validate_artifact.py <file>.html` with zero ERRORS (accessibility warnings are acceptable) — covers font sizes, gray text, undefined tokens, duplicate ids, broken in-page links, and demo-placeholder leaks
Uses the skill's brand palette (accent from brand.md), not placeholder accents; no AI-slop tells (purple/violet gradients, everything centered, Inter font, uniformly rounded corners)
Code blocks FOLLOW the theme via the --code-* tokens — light surface in light mode, dark surface in dark mode; code is not pinned to a fixed-dark panel

Depth is lossless: every piece of source detail (reasoning, options, tradeoffs, specifics, diagrams) stays REACHABLE in the output via progressive disclosure (tldr-card up front, details-fold for depth); nothing is summarized away
The run summary ends with a component inventory: every source block mapped to the component used (or prose/callout/fold) with a one-line reason

evals.name: migration-options-comparison
evals.prompt: We're deciding how to move our monolith off the legacy billing service and I need to bring three options to the team: (A) lift-and-shift the existing code onto the new platform as-is, (B) re-architect billing into its own service with a clean API, (C) a hybrid where we strangle it module by module. Each has different cost, risk, and timeline tradeoffs. Capture this as an HTML artifact people can use to compare the three side by side and pick one — not three paragraphs they read in order.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html composed from the component library: the three options side-by-side in comparison-matrix across the shared axes cost/risk/timeline, with a recommendation and the reasoning kept reachable.

assertions.text: Routes the three options to the comparison-matrix component (shared axes), not plain prose or pros-cons
All three options are present (lift-and-shift shown)
The strangler/hybrid option is present
Cost, risk, and timeline appear as shared comparison axes across all three options (rows or columns), so they can be compared on the same scales
A recommendation is stated with its reasoning — the page helps the team pick, not just list

evals.name: outage-postmortem
evals.prompt: Last night our payment service fell over for about 40 minutes — it OOM-killed under a traffic spike at 22:14, health checks started failing, we failed over to the backup pool at 22:38 and were fully recovered by 22:54. I've got the rough timeline and a couple of log excerpts. Write this up as a proper post-mortem HTML artifact I can circulate: what happened minute by minute, what we saw, root cause, and the follow-up actions.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html post-mortem: headline impact up front (stat-cards or tldr-card), a minute-by-minute timeline component with the key timestamps, log excerpts in code-block, root cause, and follow-up actions as steps/checklist.

assertions.text: Routes the chronology to the timeline component
Key timestamp 22:14 (OOM kill) present
Key timestamp 22:38 (failover) present
Key timestamp 22:54 (recovered) present
Headline impact (40-minute outage, trigger) is visible at a glance via stat-cards or tldr-card, not buried mid-page
Root cause and follow-up actions are present; follow-ups read as an actionable checklist/steps, not vague intentions
Log excerpts render in theme-following code blocks, not plain paragraphs

evals.name: backlog-triage-editor
evals.prompt: I've got a backlog of about 20 tickets for next quarter's planning and I need to sort them into Now / Next / Later / Cut. I'd rather drag them around than describe an ordering in text. Make me a little HTML tool where I can move each ticket into a bucket, and when I'm done give me a way to get the final ordering back out as text I can paste into the planning doc. Here are the tickets: search autocomplete, SSO login, dark mode, invoice PDF export, rate limiting, mobile nav redesign, audit log, bulk user import, webhook retries, 2FA, CSV export, in-app notifications, API v2, password reset flow, team roles, usage dashboard, email digests, onboarding checklist, data retention settings, GDPR delete.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html where the WHOLE artifact is the triage-board page pattern (not a composed document): Now/Next/Later/Cut buckets, all ~20 tickets draggable, export-to-text/markdown.

assertions.text: Recognizes the whole artifact is one interactive tool and uses the triage-board page pattern
Ticket 'GDPR delete' present (sample that tickets survived)
Ticket 'webhook retries' present (sample that tickets survived)
All four buckets Now / Next / Later / Cut exist and all ~20 named tickets are present as movable items
Tickets can be moved between buckets (drag-and-drop or an equivalent wired interaction)
An export/copy action emits the final ordering as paste-able text/markdown

evals.name: longform-auth-refactor
evals.prompt: Capture these findings as an HTML artifact: a narrative write-up of our week-long auth refactor — the background, what we changed across five areas, the reasoning and tradeoffs behind each decision, two mermaid diagrams of the new token flow, and open questions. It's long-form and meant to be read top to bottom with a table of contents.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html composed onto the shell as a long-form document: sidebar TOC (top-level entries plus sub-entries for dense sections), per-area reasoning behind details-folds, both mermaid blocks pre-rendered to dual-theme inline SVG via scripts/render_diagrams.py.

assertions.text: Composed as a long-form document with a sidebar TOC (this is a document, not a page pattern)
TOC has sub-entries for dense sections
Mermaid diagrams are pre-rendered inline figures, never CDN mermaid at view time
Per-decision depth uses details-fold
Depth is lossless: the reasoning/tradeoffs behind each of the five areas stays reachable behind folds, not summarized away
Each mermaid figure has a light and a dark SVG variant so it reads in both themes

evals.name: ascii-diagram-learning-doc
evals.prompt: Render the markdown file evals/fixtures/rung-mini.md into an HTML artifact (same base name, .html).
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html rendering of the fixture: the ASCII diagram converted to an embedded Excalidraw scene (SVG by default, live-canvas toggle, ASCII fallback), the comparison table as data-table, the command in code-block, the <!-- more --> depth as a details-fold, vocabulary kept lossless.

assertions.text: The ASCII diagram becomes an embedded Excalidraw scene with the ASCII fallback preserved
The comparison table routes to data-table
The command/example routes to code-block
The <!-- more --> depth routes to details-fold
The Excalidraw scene faithfully converts the ASCII diagram: same boxes (web client, API server, database) and arrows, labels inside their shapes, nothing overlapping
With the CDN unreachable the page still shows the original ASCII diagram in the fallback <pre> (verify by inspecting the fallback markup or by loading offline)

evals.name: pr-review-diff
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html PR review: the diff rendered in diff-viewer with add/remove styling, findings annotated onto the lines they refer to and color-coded by severity (high/medium/low), the retry/backoff explanation given the most depth (annotated-code).

assertions.text: The diff routes to the diff-viewer component
The thundering-herd / jitter finding is present
The actual diff renders with added/removed line styling, not quoted as plain text
Each finding is attached to the diff line(s) it refers to (inline or margin annotation), color-coded or labelled by severity — not a detached list at the end
The retry/backoff logic gets the deepest treatment (e.g. annotated-code walking the loop), matching the user's stated focus

evals.name: routing-gauntlet
evals.prompt: Render the markdown file evals/fixtures/gauntlet.md into an HTML artifact (same base name, .html).
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html where EVERY block of the dense fixture lands on its proper component: tldr-card, stat-cards, data-table (exact latency), chart (trend + before/after — the shape blocks), comparison-matrix (session-store decision), pros-cons (no-common-scale pair), timeline (incident), steps (runbook), checklist (follow-ups), glossary, quote, callout (flush warning), details-fold (option depth), tabs (per-platform install), code-block, diff-viewer, annotated-code, file-tree, diagram-excalidraw (ASCII sketch), diagram-mermaid (token flow), flowchart (deploy pipeline), figure (Figure 1). No page pattern — this is a composed document.

assertions.text: TL;DR up front
Week-in-numbers KPIs → stat-cards
Exact latency table → data-table
Trend + before/after blocks → chart
Session-store decision → comparison-matrix
No-common-scale pair → pros-cons
Incident chronology → timeline
Rollout runbook → steps
Follow-up actions → checklist
Vocabulary → glossary
Attributed Gemini quotation → quote
Flush warning → callout (visible, not folded)
Per-option depth → details-fold
Per-platform install → tabs
CLI example → code-block
Merged retry fix → diff-viewer
Backoff walkthrough → annotated-code
Repo layout → file-tree
ASCII system sketch → diagram-excalidraw
Token-flow mermaid → pre-rendered figure
Deploy pipeline with per-stage detail → flowchart
Load-test export → numbered figure
Not a page pattern (composed document, not a tool)
Depth is lossless across the whole fixture — every block's real content (numbers, names, timestamps, owners) is present and reachable
The page is not all chrome: prose reading flow still carries the narrative between components (polish pass, weight balance)

evals.name: routing-borderline
evals.prompt: Render the markdown file evals/fixtures/borderline.md into an HTML artifact (same base name, .html).
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html where each deliberately borderline block picks the RIGHT component over its neighbor: sequence-without-timestamps → steps NOT timeline; options-without-shared-axes → pros-cons NOT comparison-matrix; eight metrics → data-table NOT stat-cards; must-not-miss warning → callout NOT details-fold.

assertions.text: Migration sequence → steps
…not timeline (no timestamps worth showing)
Hosting options → pros-cons
…not comparison-matrix (no shared axes)
Eight metrics → data-table
…not stat-cards (more than 5 numbers)
Flush warning → callout
…not details-fold (must be visible on first read)
